title: Remote Versus Local Impacts of Energy Backscatter on the North Atlantic SST Biases in a Global Ocean Model
processes: Gulf Stream separation and North Atlantic Current pathways
Bottom vortex stretching and topography-flow interactions
parameterization_target: Subgrid ocean mesoscale eddy kinetic energy backscatter / eddy momentum forcing
code_availability: The data and scripts used to generate the figures are available at the Zenodo repository, Chang et al. (2023) at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.8408242.
testbed_rationale: The study analyzes physics-based energy backscatter parameterizations in 1/4° ocean simulations without machine learning, and the published Zenodo repository contains processed figure-generation data rather than model benchmarking training/test suites for ML parameterizations.
pain_points: Persistent North Atlantic SST biases (cold bias east of Flemish Cap, warm bias along the US East Coast) across climate models.
Difficulty in distinguishing local versus remote mechanisms driving circulation improvements under resolution refinement.
Nonlinear interactions and complex vorticity balances in the intergyre region hindering attribution of eddy vs. mean flow effects.
extraction_notes: The paper investigates a deterministic physical parameterization (Laplacian antiviscosity following Jansen et al., 2019) rather than an ML-based parameterization, though it discusses stochastic and eddy-closure frameworks relevant to physics-informed/ML eddy parameterization research.
